at narre.explanation: "At narre" means "to fool / trick", to make someone believe something that is not true, often for fun or in a small way. It is milder than at snyde (to cheat): at narre sine venner (to fool your friends).

sentence.da: Han forsøgte at **narre** mig med et falsk navn.
sentence.en: He tried to fool me with a fake name.

at navngive.explanation: "At navngive" means "to name", to give something an official name. It is used for a child, a ship or a new discovery. In daily talk Danes more often say at kalde (to call).

sentence.da: Forskerne vil **navngive** den nye art efter hende.
sentence.en: The researchers want to name the new species after her.

at nedbryde.explanation: "At nedbryde" means "to break down" into smaller parts through a natural process: Bakterier nedbryder affald (Bacteria break down waste). It is also used for ideas: nedbryde fordomme (break down prejudices).

sentence.da: Svampe hjælper med at **nedbryde** døde blade i skoven.
sentence.en: Fungi help break down dead leaves in the forest.

at nedkæmpe.explanation: "At nedkæmpe" means "to defeat" or "to suppress", used when you act against something until it is under control or gone: nedkæmpe et oprør (put down a rebellion), nedkæmpe en sygdom (stamp out a disease).

sentence.da: Politiet skal **nedkæmpe** den voksende kriminalitet i området.
sentence.en: The police must bring the growing crime in the area under control.

at nedlægge.explanation: "At nedlægge" means "to shut down" something for good, such as a shop, a factory or a bus line: nedlægge en buslinje (shut down a bus line). Unlike at lukke (to close), which may be just for the night, it is permanent. It also means to lay something down: nedlægge en krans (lay a wreath).

forms.en: I have shut down / laid down

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **nedlægge** den lille skole, fordi der er for få børn.
sentence.en: The city will shut down the small school because there are too few children.

at nedsætte.explanation: "At nedsætte" means "to reduce": to cut a number, a speed or a level: nedsætte farten (reduce speed). It has a second meaning, to set up a group: nedsætte en arbejdsgruppe (set up a working group).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **nedsætte** priserne på alle jakker.
sentence.en: The store will reduce the prices on all jackets.

at nedtone.explanation: "At nedtone" means "to downplay": to make something sound less important or serious than it is: Chefen nedtonede problemet (The boss downplayed the problem). It is built from ned (down) and tone (tone), like turning the volume down.

sentence.da: Man bør ikke **nedtone** faren, når børn leger ved vandet.
sentence.en: You should not downplay the danger when children play by the water.

at nikke.explanation: "At nikke" means "to nod", to move your head down and up, usually to say yes. The opposite is at ryste på hovedet (to shake your head).

sentence.da: Hun begyndte at **nikke**, da han forklarede planen.
sentence.en: She began to nod when he explained the plan.

at nippe.explanation: "At nippe" means "to sip": to take small amounts of a drink slowly, for pleasure. It is used with til: nippe til teen (sip the tea).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bare **nippe** til vinen, for jeg skal køre.
sentence.en: I will just sip the wine because I have to drive.

at notere.explanation: "At notere" means "to note down", writing something short so you remember it: Jeg noterer adressen (I note down the address).

sentence.da: Kan du **notere** mit telefonnummer?
sentence.en: Can you note down my phone number?

at nusse.explanation: "At nusse" means "to cuddle / stroke", to touch someone or an animal gently and lovingly. It is the soft touch you give a cat, a dog or a small child.

sentence.da: Børnene vil gerne **nusse** den lille hvalp.
sentence.en: The children would like to cuddle the little puppy.

at nyde.explanation: "At nyde" means "to enjoy", slowly and on purpose: Hun nyder sin kaffe (She is enjoying her coffee).

sentence.da: Vi vil **nyde** solen i parken i dag.
sentence.en: We want to enjoy the sun in the park today.

at nyse.explanation: "At nyse" means "to sneeze": Jeg nyser hele tiden (I sneeze all the time). Do not mix it up with at hoste (to cough).

sentence.da: Jeg er forkølet og må **nyse** hele tiden.
sentence.en: I have a cold and have to sneeze all the time.

at nytte.explanation: "At nytte" means "to be of use", to have an effect or make a difference. It is mostly used when something does not work: Det nytter ikke (It is no use).

sentence.da: Det vil ikke **nytte** at råbe til ham.
sentence.en: It will not help to shout at him.

at nå.explanation: "At nå" means "to reach", and also "to make it" in time: Jeg nåede det ikke (I did not make it). It also works for getting somewhere: Vi nåede hjem (We got home).

sentence.da: Jeg må løbe for at **nå** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to run to catch the bus.

at nå det.explanation: "At nå det" means "to make it", meaning to be in time: Tror du, vi når det? (Do you think we will make it?) With a thing, drop det (it): Jeg nåede bussen (I caught the bus).

sentence.da: Toget går om fem minutter, men vi kan **nå det**.
sentence.en: The train leaves in five minutes, but we can make it.

at nå toget.explanation: "At nå toget" means "to catch the train", arriving in time for it. Add ikke (not) if you are too late: Jeg nåede ikke toget (I missed the train).

sentence.da: Vi skal løbe for at **nå toget**.
sentence.en: We have to run to catch the train.

at nægte.explanation: "At nægte" means "to refuse": Han nægter at komme (He refuses to come). It also means "to deny": Hun nægter, at hun tog den (She denies that she took it).

sentence.da: Du kan **nægte** at svare.
sentence.en: You can refuse to answer.

at nærme sig.explanation: "At nærme sig" means "to approach", and sig changes with the person: Vi nærmer os byen (We are approaching the city). It works for time too: Julen nærmer sig (Christmas is getting closer).

sentence.da: Katten vil **nærme sig** fuglen langsomt.
sentence.en: The cat will approach the bird slowly.

at nævne.explanation: "At nævne" means "to mention", saying something briefly in passing: Hun nævnte det ikke (She did not mention it).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **nævne** det for ham.
sentence.en: You must not mention it to him.

at nøjes med.explanation: "At nøjes med" means "to make do with", to accept less than you wanted and be fine with it. The thing you accept comes after med: Vi nøjes med en lille bil (We make do with a small car).

sentence.da: Vi må **nøjes med** én kop kaffe i dag.
sentence.en: We must make do with one cup of coffee today.

at nøle.explanation: "At nøle" means "to hesitate", to wait a moment because you are unsure. Say what you hesitate to do with med at: Han nølede med at svare (He hesitated to answer).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **nøle**, hvis du har brug for hjælp.
sentence.en: You should not hesitate if you need help.

en nabo.explanation: "En nabo" means "a neighbor", for a man or a woman.

sentence.da: Min **nabo** bor ved siden af.
sentence.en: My neighbor lives next door.

en nakke.explanation: "En nakke" means "the back of the neck" (the nape). The front of the neck is en hals (a throat / neck).

sentence.da: Jeg har en stiv **nakke** efter en lang bilkørsel.
sentence.en: I have a stiff neck after a long drive.

en narkoman.explanation: "En narkoman" means "a drug addict", a person who is addicted to drugs. It can sound harsh, so in care work you more often hear en misbruger (a person with a substance problem).

sentence.da: En **narkoman** er afhængig af stoffer og har brug for hjælp.
sentence.en: A drug addict is dependent on drugs and needs help.

en nat.explanation: "En nat" means "a night", the dark time when most people sleep. Common phrases are i nat (tonight or last night), om natten (at night) and godnat (good night).

sentence.da: En **nat** varer fra aften til morgen.
sentence.en: A night lasts from evening to morning.

en nation.explanation: "En nation" means "a nation", a country seen as one people. It is also in the name De Forenede Nationer (the United Nations).

sentence.da: Danmark er en lille **nation** i Europa.
sentence.en: Denmark is a small nation in Europe.

en nationalbank.explanation: "En nationalbank" means "a central bank", the main bank of a country, a bank for the other banks and the state. It is not for ordinary customers: you do not have an account there.

sentence.da: Landets **nationalbank** bestemmer renten og udsteder pengene.
sentence.en: The country's central bank sets the interest rate and issues the money.

en nationalitet.explanation: "En nationalitet" means "a nationality", which country you belong to. You can ask Hvilken nationalitet har du? (What nationality are you?) and answer Jeg er dansk (I am Danish).

sentence.da: Min mand har en anden **nationalitet** end mig.
sentence.en: My husband has a different nationality than me.

en nationalpark.explanation: "En nationalpark" means "a national park", a large nature area protected by the country.

sentence.da: I en **nationalpark** beskytter man dyr og natur.
sentence.en: In a national park, animals and nature are protected.

en natklub.explanation: "En natklub" means "a nightclub", a place with music and dancing late at night. It is built from nat (night) and klub (club). Nat also gives i nat (tonight, last night).

sentence.da: Vi danser hele natten i en **natklub** i byen.
sentence.en: We dance all night in a nightclub in town.

en natlampe.explanation: "En natlampe" means "a bedside lamp", a small lamp that gives soft light at night. It is built from nat (night) and lampe (lamp). The same nat is in en natkjole (a nightgown).

sentence.da: Jeg har en lille **natlampe** ved min seng.
sentence.en: I have a small bedside lamp by my bed.

en nattesøvn.explanation: "En nattesøvn" means "a night's sleep", the sleep you get during one night. You use it to say how much or how well you slept: en god nattesøvn (a good night's sleep).

sentence.da: De fleste voksne har brug for syv timers **nattesøvn**.
sentence.en: Most adults need seven hours of sleep a night.

en naturkatastrofe.explanation: "En naturkatastrofe" means "a natural disaster", a sudden event in nature that destroys homes and lives. It is built from natur (nature) and katastrofe (a disaster).

sentence.da: En oversvømmelse eller et jordskælv kan være en **naturkatastrofe**.
sentence.en: A flood or an earthquake can be a natural disaster.

en naturvejleder.explanation: "En naturvejleder" means "a nature guide", a person who takes groups outdoors and explains what they see, such as plants, animals and landscape.

sentence.da: En **naturvejleder** fortæller om dyrene og planterne i skoven.
sentence.en: A nature guide tells about the animals and plants in the forest.

en navle.explanation: "En navle" means "a navel", the small round dent in the middle of your front, where you were joined to your mother before birth.

sentence.da: Barnet har en lille **navle** midt på maven.
sentence.en: The child has a small navel in the middle of the stomach.

en navngivning.explanation: "En navngivning" means "a naming", the act of giving a name to a person, a place, an animal or a thing. It comes from at navngive (to name).

sentence.da: Ved **navngivning** af en ny art bruger forskere ofte latin.
sentence.en: When naming a new species, scientists often use Latin.

en nederdel.explanation: "En nederdel" means "a skirt", clothing that hangs from the waist. It is built from neder (down) and del (part), so it literally means a lower part. Del alone means a part: en del af byen (a part of the town).

sentence.da: Hun tager en **nederdel** på, ikke bukser.
sentence.en: She puts on a skirt, not pants.

en nedgang.explanation: "En nedgang" means "a decline", a fall in size, number or level: en nedgang i priserne (a decline in prices). It is also a way down to a lower place, such as nedgangen til metroen (the way down to the metro).

sentence.da: Der var en **nedgang** i antallet af turister i år.
sentence.en: There was a decline in the number of tourists this year.

en nedskæring.explanation: "En nedskæring" means "a cutback", less money, staff or service than before, often at a company or in public services. It comes from at skære ned (to cut back).

sentence.da: Skolen står over for en stor **nedskæring** i budgettet.
sentence.en: The school faces a big cutback in its budget.

en negl.explanation: "En negl" means "a nail" on a finger or toe. A metal nail you hit with a hammer is a different word, et søm (a metal nail), so do not mix them up.

sentence.da: Jeg har knækket en **negl** på min finger.
sentence.en: I have broken a nail on my finger.

en neglesalon.explanation: "En neglesalon" means "a nail salon", where you get a manicure. To say what you are doing there, use Jeg skal have lavet negle (I am getting my nails done).

sentence.da: I en **neglesalon** kan man få lakeret sine negle.
sentence.en: In a nail salon you can get your nails polished.

en nerve.explanation: "En nerve" means "a nerve", a thin fiber that carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body. The plural also appears in an idiom for being annoyed: Støjen går mig på nerverne (The noise gets on my nerves).

sentence.da: En **nerve** sender signaler fra hjernen til musklerne.
sentence.en: A nerve sends signals from the brain to the muscles.

en nevø.explanation: "En nevø" means "a nephew", your brother's or sister's son. The female version is en niece (a niece).

sentence.da: Min **nevø** kalder mig onkel.
sentence.en: My nephew calls me uncle.

en niece.explanation: "En niece" means "a niece", your brother's or sister's daughter. The male version is en nevø (a nephew).

sentence.da: Min **niece** kalder mig tante.
sentence.en: My niece calls me aunt.

en nisse.explanation: "En nisse" means "a Christmas elf", a small Danish folklore creature in a red cap. He plays tricks if people do not treat him well.

sentence.da: Børnene satte risengrød frem til den lille **nisse**.
sentence.en: The children put out rice porridge for the little elf.

en nordmand.explanation: "En nordmand" means "a Norwegian", a person from Norway. The country is Norge.

sentence.da: Hun er **nordmand** og bor i Oslo.
sentence.en: She is Norwegian and lives in Oslo.

en norm.explanation: "En norm" means "a norm", a shared expectation of how people behave in a group or a country. Nobody writes it down, but people notice when it is broken.

sentence.da: I Danmark er det en **norm** at komme til tiden.
sentence.en: In Denmark it is a norm to arrive on time.

en note.explanation: "En note" means "a note", a few words written down to remember or tell something.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en **note** på køleskabet.
sentence.en: I put a note on the fridge.

en notesbog.explanation: "En notesbog" means "a notebook" for writing by hand. It ends in bog (book), like en ordbog (a dictionary) and en lærebog (a textbook).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver nye ord i min **notesbog**.
sentence.en: I write new words in my notebook.

en novelle.explanation: "En novelle" means "a short story", a short piece of fiction that you can read in one sitting, usually built around a single event.

sentence.da: En **novelle** er meget kortere end en roman.
sentence.en: A short story is much shorter than a novel.

en nuance.explanation: "En nuance" means "a nuance", a very small variation in meaning, opinion or color that is easy to miss.

sentence.da: Der er en lille **nuance** i betydningen af de to ord.
sentence.en: There is a small nuance in the meaning of the two words.

en nummerplade.explanation: "En nummerplade" means "a license plate". It is nummer (number) plus plade (plate). Plade also means a record, as in en vinylplade (a vinyl record).

sentence.da: Hvad er nummeret på din **nummerplade**?
sentence.en: What is the number on your license plate?

en nyhed.explanation: "En nyhed" means "a piece of news", one single item: Det er en dårlig nyhed (That is bad news). For the news on TV, Danes use the plural: Nyhederne begynder nu (The news is starting now).

sentence.da: Jeg har en god **nyhed** til dig.
sentence.en: I have good news for you.

en nyhedsside.explanation: "En nyhedsside" means "a news site", a website that publishes news and updates it through the day. Side means both page and site, so for one page in a printed paper say en avisside (a newspaper page).

sentence.da: På en **nyhedsside** kan man følge med i dagens begivenheder.
sentence.en: On a news site you can keep up with the events of the day.

en nyhedsudsendelse.explanation: "En nyhedsudsendelse" means "a news broadcast", a program on television or radio that reports what has happened, at a set time. Udsendelse (a broadcast) is any program, and nyheds- (news-) says what kind.

sentence.da: I en **nyhedsudsendelse** hører man, hvad der er sket i dag.
sentence.en: In a news broadcast you hear what has happened today.

en nyhedsvært.explanation: "En nyhedsvært" means "a news anchor", the person who sits in the studio, presents the main stories and introduces the others. Vært (a host) alone is the host of any show or event.

sentence.da: En **nyhedsvært** præsenterer dagens vigtigste historier i studiet.
sentence.en: A news anchor presents the day's most important stories in the studio.

en nyre.explanation: "En nyre" means "a kidney", one of two bean-shaped organs in your lower back. You can live with just one, so people can donate one to someone else.

sentence.da: En **nyre** renser blodet og laver urin.
sentence.en: A kidney cleans the blood and makes urine.

en nytårskur.explanation: "En nytårskur" means "a New Year's reception", a get-together in early January, usually held by a company or an organization, with drinks and short talks. Guests come to wish each other a happy new year.

sentence.da: Firmaet inviterer alle kunder til sin årlige **nytårskur** i januar.
sentence.en: The company invites all customers to its annual New Year's reception in January.

en nål.explanation: "En nål" means "a needle", a thin pointed tool. It also covers other thin pointed things, like en nål til en grammofon (a needle for a record player).

sentence.da: Lægen stikker en **nål** i min arm.
sentence.en: The doctor sticks a needle in my arm.

en næse.explanation: "En næse" means "a nose", the part in the middle of your face used for breathing. You can say Jeg har en løbende næse (I have a runny nose). At have næse for noget (to have a nose for something) means to have a good feel for it.

sentence.da: Jeg kan lugte blomsten med min **næse**.
sentence.en: I can smell the flower with my nose.

en næsespray.explanation: "En næsespray" means "a nasal spray", a small bottle that you spray into your nose when it is stuffed up.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **næsespray**, når næsen er tilstoppet.
sentence.en: I use nasal spray when my nose is blocked.

en nød.explanation: "En nød" means "a nut". The same spelling also means distress, as in Han er i nød (He is in distress).

sentence.da: Egernet gemmer en **nød** til vinteren.
sentence.en: The squirrel saves a nut for the winter.

en nøddeallergi.explanation: "En nøddeallergi" means "a nut allergy", a reaction of the body against nuts, which can be dangerous even in small amounts. Food labels warn about it: Kan indeholde spor af nødder (May contain traces of nuts).

sentence.da: Han har **nøddeallergi** og må ikke spise mandler.
sentence.en: He has a nut allergy and must not eat almonds.

en nødsituation.explanation: "En nødsituation" means "an emergency", a sudden and dangerous situation where people need help right away.

sentence.da: Ring til 112, når der er en **nødsituation**.
sentence.en: Call 112 when there is an emergency.

en nødudgang.explanation: "En nødudgang" means "an emergency exit", the door you use when there is danger.

sentence.da: Døren er en **nødudgang**, og den må ikke låses.
sentence.en: The door is an emergency exit and must not be locked.

en nødvendighed.explanation: "En nødvendighed" means "a necessity", something you must have, not just something you would like. The word for something being needed is nødvendig (necessary).

sentence.da: Rent vand er en **nødvendighed**, men ikke alle har det.
sentence.en: Clean water is a necessity, but not everyone has it.

en nøgle.explanation: "En nøgle" means "a key", a small metal tool that opens and locks a door.

sentence.da: Jeg åbner døren med min **nøgle**.
sentence.en: I open the door with my key.

en nøglering.explanation: "En nøglering" means "a key ring", the ring that holds your keys together.

sentence.da: Jeg har otte nøgler på min **nøglering**.
sentence.en: I have eight keys on my key ring.

en nørd.explanation: "En nørd" means "a nerd", someone very keen on one topic. Put the topic in front: en computernørd (a computer nerd), en filmnørd (a movie nerd).

sentence.da: Min bror er en **nørd** og elsker computere.
sentence.en: My brother is a nerd and loves computers.

et nabolag.explanation: "Et nabolag" means "a neighborhood", the area around your home and the people in it. It is built on nabo (neighbor).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et rart **nabolag** nær skolen.
sentence.en: We live in a nice neighborhood near the school.

et naboskab.explanation: "Et naboskab" means "a neighborhood relationship", the way people who live close to each other get along. It describes the relationship, not the people themselves, who are naboer (neighbors).

sentence.da: Et godt **naboskab** betyder, at man hjælper hinanden.
sentence.en: A good neighborhood relationship means that people help each other.

et natbord.explanation: "Et natbord" means "a nightstand". It is nat (night) plus bord (table), and it stands next to the bed.

sentence.da: Jeg har en lampe og en bog på mit **natbord**.
sentence.en: I have a lamp and a book on my nightstand.

et naturområde.explanation: "Et naturområde" means "a nature area", a stretch of land or water with wild plants and animals, often kept as it is so that people can visit it.

sentence.da: Vi går tur i et stort **naturområde** med sø og skov.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in a large nature area with a lake and forest.

et navn.explanation: "Et navn" means "a name". To ask someone's name, Danes usually say Hvad hedder du? (literally, What are you called?).

sentence.da: Hvad er dit **navn**?
sentence.en: What is your name?

et navneord.explanation: "Et navneord" means "a noun", a word that names something, like bil (a car) or Anna. Teachers also say et substantiv, which means the same.

sentence.da: **Navneord** er ord for personer, steder og ting.
sentence.en: Nouns are words for people, places and things.

et nedbrud.explanation: "Et nedbrud" means "a crash", when a computer or system suddenly stops working. It is built from ned (down) and brud (break), and brud also appears in et benbrud (a broken bone).

sentence.da: Efter et **nedbrud** skal jeg starte computeren igen.
sentence.en: After a crash, I have to start the computer again.

et nederlag.explanation: "Et nederlag" means "a defeat", being beaten in a game, a war or an election.

sentence.da: Holdet tabte 5-0, og alle kaldte det et stort **nederlag**.
sentence.en: The team lost 5-0, and everyone called it a big defeat.

et net.explanation: "Et net" means "a net": et net på tennisbanen (a net on the tennis court). With the ending, nettet means "the internet": Jeg søger på nettet (I am searching on the internet).

sentence.da: Han fangede en stor fisk i sit **net**.
sentence.en: He caught a big fish in his net.

et netværk.explanation: "Et netværk" means "a network", a group of connected computers or people: et netværk af kolleger (a network of colleagues).

sentence.da: Vores computere er på det samme **netværk**.
sentence.en: Our computers are on the same network.

et nik.explanation: "Et nik" means "a nod", a small movement of the head, up and down, that means yes.

sentence.da: Hun svarede med et **nik** og smilede.
sentence.en: She answered with a nod and smiled.

et niveau.explanation: "Et niveau" means "a level", how high or advanced something is: Vi har tre niveauer: begynder, mellem og avanceret (We have three levels: beginner, intermediate and advanced).

sentence.da: Han spiller tennis på et højt **niveau**.
sentence.en: He plays tennis at a high level.

et nummer.explanation: "Et nummer" means "a number" used as a label, such as a phone number or a house number. For counting or amounts, use et tal (a number, a figure) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dit **nummer**.
sentence.en: I call your number.

et nyhedsbrev.explanation: "Et nyhedsbrev" means "a newsletter", a letter or email that a company or club sends regularly to people who signed up. You join with at tilmelde sig (to sign up) and stop it with at afmelde sig (to unsubscribe).

sentence.da: Butikken sender et **nyhedsbrev** med nye tilbud hver måned.
sentence.en: The store sends a newsletter with new offers every month.

et nyhedsprogram.explanation: "Et nyhedsprogram" means "a news program", a show on television or radio that reports what has happened that day. The first part, nyheds-, comes from nyheder (news).

sentence.da: I et **nyhedsprogram** fortæller en vært om dagens vigtigste begivenheder.
sentence.en: In a news program, a host tells about the most important events of the day.

et nys.explanation: "Et nys" means "a sneeze", the sudden burst of air through the nose. The action is at nyse (to sneeze): Jeg skal nyse (I have to sneeze).

sentence.da: Hun gav et højt **nys**, og alle kiggede på hende.
sentence.en: She gave a loud sneeze, and everyone looked at her.

et nytår.explanation: "Et nytår" means "a New Year", the time around January 1: Godt nytår! (Happy New Year!) You can also say holde nytår (to celebrate New Year).

sentence.da: Ved **nytår** ser vi fyrværkeri.
sentence.en: At New Year, we watch fireworks.

et næb.explanation: "Et næb" means "a beak", the hard, pointed mouth of a bird. Unlike a mouth, it has no lips or teeth.

sentence.da: Fuglen bruger sit **næb** til at samle mad op.
sentence.en: The bird uses its beak to pick up food.

et nødopkald.explanation: "Et nødopkald" means "an emergency call", a phone call to ask the rescue services for help right away. It is only for real danger, not for ordinary questions.

sentence.da: Man foretager et **nødopkald** til 112, når nogen er i fare.
sentence.en: You make an emergency call to 112 when someone is in danger.

et nødstilfælde.explanation: "Et nødstilfælde" means "an emergency", a sudden situation where someone needs help at once. Signs often use it after i (in): Brug døren i nødstilfælde (Use the door in an emergency).

sentence.da: Når nogen holder op med at trække vejret, er det et **nødstilfælde**.
sentence.en: When someone stops breathing, it is an emergency.

et nøglekort.explanation: "Et nøglekort" means "a key card", a plastic card that opens a door instead of a key, for example at a hotel.

sentence.da: Hotellet giver mig et **nøglekort** til værelset.
sentence.en: The hotel gives me a key card for the room.

naiv.explanation: "Naiv" means "naive", describing someone who trusts too easily and believes things without checking. It can sound a little critical, as if the person lacks experience.

sentence.da: Jeg var **naiv**, da jeg stolede på ham.
sentence.en: I was naive when I trusted him.

narkose.explanation: "Narkose" means "anesthesia", the deep sleep a patient is put into for an operation so that they feel nothing. It is different from en lokalbedøvelse (a local anesthetic), which numbs only one spot and leaves you awake.

sentence.da: Hun lå i **narkose** under hele operationen.
sentence.en: She was under anesthesia during the whole operation.

narkotika.explanation: "Narkotika" means "narcotics", illegal things like heroin and cocaine that people take to get high. It is used for them as a group, with no en or et in front of it.

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at sælge **narkotika**.
sentence.en: It is illegal to sell narcotics.

national.explanation: "National" means "national", for something that belongs to a whole country, such as Denmark. The opposite is lokal (local): en lokal avis (a local paper).

sentence.da: Fodbold er en **national** passion i mange lande.
sentence.en: Soccer is a national passion in many countries.

nato.explanation: "NATO" means "NATO", the military group of nations that promise to defend each other.

sentence.da: Danmark har været med i **NATO** i mange år.
sentence.en: Denmark has been in NATO for many years.

natur.explanation: "Natur" means "nature", the outdoors with forests, lakes and animals.

sentence.da: Danmark har smuk **natur**.
sentence.en: Denmark has beautiful nature.

naturgas.explanation: "En naturgas" means "natural gas", gas taken from the ground and used for heating, cooking and making power. It is built from natur (nature) and en gas (a gas).

forms.en: The price of natural gas is rising

sentence.da: Mange huse bliver opvarmet med **naturgas**.
sentence.en: Many houses are heated with natural gas.

naturlig.explanation: "Naturlig" means "natural", normal and as expected: Det er helt naturligt at være nervøs (It is completely natural to be nervous). It also means found in the world as it is, not made by people: naturlige materialer (natural materials).

sentence.da: Hun har en **naturlig** evne til at tegne.
sentence.en: She has a natural ability to draw.

naturligvis.explanation: "Naturligvis" means "of course", and it also works alone as a reply: Kan du hjælpe? Naturligvis! (Can you help? Of course!)

sentence.da: **Naturligvis** hjælper jeg dig i morgen.
sentence.en: Of course I will help you tomorrow.

navnemåde.explanation: "En navnemåde" means "the plain form of a verb", the one with at in front, like at spise (to eat). It is built from et navn (a name) and en måde (a way), because this form only names the action.

sentence.da: Verbet at gå står i **navnemåde**.
sentence.en: The verb at gå is in its plain form.

navnlig.explanation: "Navnlig" means "especially" or "in particular", and it picks out the strongest example from a larger group. You put it right before that example.

sentence.da: Mange kan lide frugt, **navnlig** æbler.
sentence.en: Many people like fruit, especially apples.

ned.explanation: "Ned" means "down", for moving down. Compare Kom ned! (Come down!) with Han er nede i kælderen (He is down in the cellar). Nede says where someone is, ned says where someone is going.

sentence.da: Elevatoren går op og **ned**.
sentence.en: The elevator goes up and down.

nedad.explanation: "Nedad" means "downward", toward a lower place or level. It shows the direction of travel, and it also works for numbers: Priserne går nedad (Prices are going downward).

sentence.da: Vandet løber **nedad**, fordi vejen hælder.
sentence.en: The water runs downward because the road slopes.

nedenunder.explanation: "Nedenunder" means "below" or "downstairs", on the floor right under the one you are on, as in a house or an apartment building.

sentence.da: Vores nabo bor **nedenunder**.
sentence.en: Our neighbor lives downstairs.

nedslående.explanation: "Nedslående" means "disheartening", for news or results that make people feel let down and lose energy. It describes the thing, not the person; a person who feels this way is nedtrykt (downcast).

sentence.da: Resultatet var **nedslående**, men vi giver ikke op.
sentence.en: The result was disheartening, but we are not giving up.

nedtrykt.explanation: "Nedtrykt" means "downcast" or "down", feeling low in spirit for a while. It is built from ned (down) and trykt (pressed), so it is like "pressed down".

sentence.da: Efter nyheden var han **nedtrykt** i flere dage.
sentence.en: After the news he was downcast for several days.

negativ.explanation: "Negativ" means "negative" and describes a bad or gloomy view of things. In a medical test it means nothing was found: en negativ test (a negative test).

sentence.da: Han har en meget **negativ** holdning.
sentence.en: He has a very negative attitude.

neglelak.explanation: "Neglelak" means "nail polish", the colored liquid you paint on your nails. To take it off, you need neglelakfjerner (nail polish remover).

sentence.da: Hun har rød **neglelak** på fingrene.
sentence.en: She has red nail polish on her fingers.

nej.explanation: "Nej" means "no". It can also mean "oh!" when you are surprised: Nej, hvor er det flot! (Oh, how beautiful!).

sentence.da: Vil du have kaffe? **Nej**, tak.
sentence.en: Do you want coffee? No, thank you.

nem.explanation: "Nem" means "easy", for something that takes little effort to do. The opposite is svær (hard): en svær opgave (a hard task).

sentence.da: En **nem** opskrift tager kun ti minutter.
sentence.en: An easy recipe takes only ten minutes.

nemlig.explanation: "Nemlig" means "exactly" as a reply: Er du træt? Nemlig! (Are you tired? Exactly!). Inside a sentence it means "you see" and gives the reason: Jeg bliver hjemme, jeg er nemlig syg (I am staying home, I am sick, you see).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke komme, jeg er **nemlig** syg.
sentence.en: I cannot come, I am sick, you see.

nemt.explanation: "Nemt" means "easy" or "easily". It also says how something is done: Han vinder nemt (He wins easily).

sentence.da: Det er **nemt**: to plus to er fire.
sentence.en: It is easy: two plus two is four.

nervepirrende.explanation: "Nervepirrende" means "nerve-wracking": so tense that your nerves are on edge. It is built from nerve (nerve) and pirrende (stirring up), so it literally stirs up your nerves.

sentence.da: Ventetiden før eksamensresultatet var **nervepirrende**, og jeg sov dårligt.
sentence.en: The wait before the exam result was nerve-wracking, and I slept badly.

nervøs.explanation: "Nervøs" means "nervous", the feeling before something important: Jeg er nervøs før eksamen (I am nervous before the exam). The opposite is rolig (calm).

sentence.da: Han er **nervøs**, fordi han skal til tandlægen.
sentence.en: He is nervous because he has to go to the dentist.

nervøsitet.explanation: "En nervøsitet" means "nervousness", the feeling before something important. Danes more often say nervøs (nervous): Jeg er nervøs (I am nervous).

sentence.da: Man kan se hendes **nervøsitet**, når hun skal tale.
sentence.en: You can see her nervousness when she has to speak.

netop.explanation: "Netop" means "exactly" or "just". It can point at the very thing someone said, or say that something happened a moment ago.

forms.da: Det er netop, hvad jeg mente.
forms.en: That is exactly what I meant.

sentence.da: Jeg skulle **netop** til at ringe til dig.
sentence.en: I was just about to call you.

neutral.explanation: "Neutral" means "neutral", not taking a side and not standing out. It is used for a person or country that takes no side in a conflict, and for colors such as gray that go with everything.

sentence.da: Dommeren skal være **neutral** og ikke holde med nogen.
sentence.en: The referee must be neutral and not support anyone.

ni.explanation: "Ni" means "nine". Do not mix it up with nej (no): Jeg har ni børn (I have nine children) but Nej, tak (No, thank you).

sentence.da: Efter otte kommer **ni**.
sentence.en: After eight comes nine.

niende.explanation: "Niende" means "ninth": den niende dag (the ninth day). It is also used for dates: den niende maj (the ninth of May).

sentence.da: Efter den ottende dag kommer den **niende** dag.
sentence.en: After the eighth day comes the ninth day.

nitten.explanation: "Nitten" means "nineteen". Compare ni børn (nine children) with nitten børn (nineteen children). The -ten at the end is like the -teen in English nineteen.

sentence.da: Min søster er **nitten** år.
sentence.en: My sister is nineteen years old.

nogen.explanation: "Nogen" means "someone" or "anyone". After ikke (not) or in a question it means "anyone" or "any": Jeg har ikke nogen venner (I do not have any friends).

sentence.da: Der er ikke **nogen** hjemme.
sentence.en: Nobody is home.

nogenlunde.explanation: "Nogenlunde" means "fairly" or "reasonably", not perfect but good enough. On its own it works as an answer: Hvordan går det? Nogenlunde. (How is it going? So-so.)

sentence.da: Jeg taler **nogenlunde** dansk, men jeg laver stadig fejl.
sentence.en: I speak Danish reasonably well, but I still make mistakes.

nogensinde.explanation: "Nogensinde" means "ever" and mostly appears in questions. A common answer is Nej, aldrig (No, never).

sentence.da: Har du **nogensinde** været i Norge?
sentence.en: Have you ever been to Norway?

noget.explanation: "Noget" means "something" or "anything". Compare Jeg ser noget (I see something) with Jeg ser nogen (I see someone): noget is for things, nogen is for people. With things you cannot count, it means "some": noget mælk (some milk).

forms.da: Vil du have noget at spise?
forms.en: Do you want something to eat?

sentence.da: Jeg er tørstig. Har du **noget** at drikke?
sentence.en: I am thirsty. Do you have something to drink?

nogle.explanation: "Nogle" means "some" or "a few". Compare Jeg har en ven (I have one friend) with Jeg har nogle venner (I have some friends). In a question or with ikke, nogen is the usual word: Har du nogen venner? (Do you have any friends?).

sentence.da: Der er **nogle** æbler på bordet.
sentence.en: There are some apples on the table.

nogle gange.explanation: "Nogle gange" means "sometimes", or, word for word, some times. It sits in the middle between altid (always) and aldrig (never): Jeg spiser nogle gange morgenmad (I sometimes eat breakfast).

sentence.da: **Nogle gange** tager jeg bussen.
sentence.en: Sometimes I take the bus.

nok.explanation: "Nok" means "enough" and also "probably". Compare Jeg har nok mad (I have enough food) with Han kommer nok (He will probably come). The first is about how much; the second is a guess. Alone, Det er nok! (That is enough!) tells someone to stop.

forms.en: I do not have enough time.

sentence.da: Nej tak, jeg har **nok** mad.
sentence.en: No thanks, I have enough food.

nord.explanation: "Nord" means "north". Use i nord (in the north) for where something is and mod nord (toward the north) for the way you are going.

sentence.da: Kompasnålen peger mod **nord**.
sentence.en: The compass needle points north.

nordamerika.explanation: "Nordamerika" means "North America", the big area with Canada, the USA and Mexico. It is built from nord (north) and Amerika (America).

sentence.da: Hun bor i **Nordamerika**, i Canada.
sentence.en: She lives in North America, in Canada.

norden.explanation: "Norden" means "the Nordic countries": Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland, often with Greenland, the Faroe Islands and Åland. It is written with a capital N and used without an extra word in front: i Norden (in the Nordic countries).

sentence.da: Mange rejser mellem landene i **Norden** uden pas.
sentence.en: Many people travel between the countries of the Nordic region without a passport.

nordisk.explanation: "Nordisk" means "Nordic", about Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland together and what they share, such as nordisk mad (Nordic food).

sentence.da: Danmark og Sverige har en **nordisk** velfærdsmodel.
sentence.en: Denmark and Sweden have a Nordic welfare model.

nordlig.explanation: "Nordlig" means "northern", the north part of a place: Skagen ligger i det nordlige Danmark (Skagen is in northern Denmark). For wind it also means "from the north".

sentence.da: Vinden er **nordlig**, og det er koldt.
sentence.en: The wind is from the north, and it is cold.

nordlys.explanation: "Et nordlys" means "northern lights", the green and sometimes red or purple glow seen in the sky far in the north. You mostly see it in places such as Norway, Iceland and Greenland. It is built from nord (north) and et lys (a light).

sentence.da: Vi så **nordlys** over fjorden i Norge.
sentence.en: We saw northern lights over the fjord in Norway.

nordpå.explanation: "Nordpå" means "northward", toward the north. To say where something lies, use i nord (in the north): Skoven ligger i nord (The forest lies in the north).

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver **nordpå** om foråret.
sentence.en: The birds fly north in the spring.

nordsøen.explanation: "Nordsøen" means "the North Sea", the sea along the west coast of Jylland (Jutland).

sentence.da: **Nordsøen** ligger vest for Danmark.
sentence.en: The North Sea lies west of Denmark.

norge.explanation: "Norge" means "Norway". The country is Norge, but the language is norsk (Norwegian): Jeg bor i Norge og taler norsk (I live in Norway and speak Norwegian).

sentence.da: Min ven kommer fra **Norge** og taler norsk.
sentence.en: My friend comes from Norway and speaks Norwegian.

normal.explanation: "Normal" means "normal", for what is usual and as expected. It is spelled the same as in English.

sentence.da: En **normal** kropstemperatur er 37 grader.
sentence.en: A normal body temperature is 37 degrees.

norsk.explanation: "Norsk" means "Norwegian", both for things from Norway and for the language. Danish writes it with a small letter: Jeg taler norsk (I speak Norwegian).

sentence.da: I Oslo taler man **norsk**.
sentence.en: In Oslo people speak Norwegian.

nougat.explanation: "Nougat" means "nougat", a soft, sweet brown filling often found inside chocolate.

sentence.da: Man laver **nougat** af nødder og sukker.
sentence.en: You make nougat from nuts and sugar.

november.explanation: "November" means "November" and is spelled the same as in English. Danish writes month names with a small letter, even in the middle of a sentence: i november (in November).

sentence.da: Det er mørkt og gråt i **november**.
sentence.en: It is dark and gray in November.

nu.explanation: "Nu" means "now". Danes also drop nu into a sentence to soften it, with no idea of time: Det er nu ikke så svært (It is not that hard, really).

sentence.da: Jeg skal gå **nu**.
sentence.en: I have to go now.

nu skal du høre.explanation: "Nu skal du høre" means "now listen", literally "now you will hear". People say it to get attention just before telling a story or news.

forms.da: Nu skal du høre, hvad jeg har at sige.
forms.en: Now listen to what I have to say.

sentence.da: Vent, **nu skal du høre**, jeg har en god nyhed.
sentence.en: Wait, now listen, I have good news.

nudler.explanation: "Nudler" means "noodles", long thin strips of dough, boiled and eaten with sauce or vegetables.

sentence.da: Jeg koger **nudler** i vand.
sentence.en: I boil noodles in water.

nul.explanation: "Nul" means "zero". In sports scores it is "nil": Vi vinder to–nul (We win two–nil).

sentence.da: Vandet bliver til is ved **nul** grader.
sentence.en: Water turns to ice at zero degrees.

nutid.explanation: "En nutid" means "a present tense", the verb form for what is happening now: jeg løber (I run) is in nutid. Nutiden (the present) also means the present time in general.

sentence.da: Sætningen Jeg spiser et æble står i **nutid**.
sentence.en: The sentence I eat an apple is in the present tense.

nutiden.explanation: "Nutiden" means "the present", the time we live in now, often set against what came before and what comes next. Use it when you talk about modern life, as in nutidens unge (the young people of today).

sentence.da: Vi lærer om fortiden, men vi lever i **nutiden**.
sentence.en: We learn about the past, but we live in the present.

nutildags.explanation: "Nutildags" means "nowadays", used to compare now with earlier times. It is also written as three words, nu til dags (now to day), with the same meaning.

sentence.da: Før skrev vi breve, men **nutildags** skriver vi beskeder.
sentence.en: Before, we wrote letters, but nowadays we write messages.

nuttet.explanation: "Nuttet" means "cute" and is used for small things that make you smile, like babies, puppies and kittens.

sentence.da: Din lille hund er så **nuttet**.
sentence.en: Your little dog is so cute.

nuvel.explanation: "Nuvel" means "well now" or "very well". You say it to accept something or to move on to the next thing. It sounds a little formal, so in everyday talk people more often say godt (all right).

sentence.da: **Nuvel**, så er det aftalt, og vi mødes klokken ni.
sentence.en: Very well, then it is agreed, and we meet at nine.

nuværende.explanation: "Nuværende" means "current" or "present", the one that is true at this moment, as opposed to an earlier or a later one. It goes before the word it describes: den nuværende regering (the current government).

sentence.da: Min **nuværende** chef er sød, men min tidligere var streng.
sentence.en: My current boss is nice, but my former one was strict.

ny.explanation: "Ny" means "new", for something just made, just bought or not used before. It is also part of nytår (new year), as in godt nytår (happy new year).

sentence.da: Jeg har købt en **ny** telefon.
sentence.en: I have bought a new phone.

nyheder.explanation: "Nyheder" means "news". Danish treats it as plural: Nyhederne er dårlige (The news is bad; literally, the news are bad). One single piece of news is en nyhed.

sentence.da: Jeg læser **nyheder** i avisen hver morgen.
sentence.en: I read the news in the newspaper every morning.

nylig.explanation: "Nylig" means "recently" and is built from ny (new). It is almost always used in the phrase for nylig.

sentence.da: Jeg mødte hende for **nylig** i byen.
sentence.en: I met her recently in town.

nysgerrig.explanation: "Nysgerrig" means "curious" and describes someone who wants to know things: Han er nysgerrig efter at lære mere (He is curious to learn more). It can also mean nosy: Vær ikke så nysgerrig! (Don't be so nosy!)

sentence.da: Min søn er **nysgerrig** og stiller mange spørgsmål.
sentence.en: My son is curious and asks many questions.

nysgerrighed.explanation: "En nysgerrighed" means "curiosity", the wish to find out or know more. It comes from nysgerrig (curious) with -hed on the end, like -ness in English. The same ending turns fri (free) into en frihed (a freedom).

sentence.da: Børn stiller mange spørgsmål af **nysgerrighed**.
sentence.en: Children ask many questions out of curiosity.

nytte.explanation: "En nytte" means "use" or "benefit", the good you get out of something. It has no plural. Danes also say gøre nytte (to be of use) about a thing or a person that helps.

sentence.da: Jeg har stor **nytte** af min nye ordbog.
sentence.en: I get great use out of my new dictionary.

nyttig.explanation: "Nyttig" means "useful". It describes something that helps you get a job done, like a tip, a tool or a book.

sentence.da: Paraplyen er **nyttig**, når det regner.
sentence.en: The umbrella is useful when it rains.

nytårsaften.explanation: "Nytårsaften" means "New Year's Eve", the evening of 31 December. It is made from nytår (new year) and aften (evening).

sentence.da: På **nytårsaften** siger vi "godt nytår" ved midnat.
sentence.en: On New Year's Eve we say "happy new year" at midnight.

nå.explanation: "Nå" means "oh" or "well". You say it when you understand something or are a little surprised. Do not mix it up with nu (now).

sentence.da: **Nå**, nu forstår jeg det!
sentence.en: Oh, now I understand!

nå ja.explanation: "Nå ja" means "oh right" and shows you just remembered or understood something. It often comes with jo, a small word that means "as you know": Nå ja, det er jo tirsdag i dag (Oh right, it's Tuesday today, you know).

forms.da: Nå ja, nu husker jeg det.

sentence.da: **Nå ja**, jeg skal jo hente børnene.
sentence.en: Oh right, I have to pick up the kids.

nå men.explanation: "Nå men" means "well then" and you say it to move a conversation on or to wrap it up. After it you usually say what happens next, such as starting a task or leaving.

forms.da: Nå men, lad os komme i gang.

forms.en: Well then, I have to move on.

sentence.da: **Nå men**, nu må jeg hellere gå.
sentence.en: Well then, I had better go now.

nåde.explanation: "En nåde" means "mercy" or "grace": kindness shown to someone who could have been punished. The same word is used in religion for grace, and in old royal titles.

sentence.da: Fangen bad dommeren om **nåde**, men fik ingen.
sentence.en: The prisoner asked the judge for mercy, but got none.

når.explanation: "Når" means "when" for things that happen every time or have not happened yet. Compare Når det regner, bliver jeg hjemme (Whenever it rains, I stay home) with Da jeg kom hjem, var det mørkt (When I came home, it was dark). That was one time in the past, so it uses da. In a question, use hvornår: Hvornår kommer du? (When are you coming?).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer, **når** jeg kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I will call when I get home.

når som helst.explanation: "Når som helst" means "anytime", or "whenever". It can also mean "at any moment", for something that might happen without warning: Det kan regne når som helst (It can rain at any moment).

forms.da: Jeg har tid når som helst.

sentence.da: Du kan ringe til mig **når som helst**.
sentence.en: You can call me anytime.

næppe.explanation: "Næppe" means "hardly" or "barely", about what is very unlikely or only just true. A tiny chance is left, unlike aldrig (never).

forms.en: She is unlikely to come today

sentence.da: Vi får **næppe** sne, fordi det er for varmt.
sentence.en: We are unlikely to get snow because it is too warm.

nær.explanation: "Nær" means "close" or "near". It is mostly used about people you are close to, like a friend or family member. For places, tæt på (close to) is more common: tæt på stationen means "close to the station".

sentence.da: Han er en **nær** ven af mig.
sentence.en: He is a close friend of mine.

nærig.explanation: "Nærig" means "stingy", not wanting to spend or give away money even when it would be fair. It is a negative word about a person, unlike sparsommelig (thrifty), which is a good quality.

sentence.da: Han er **nærig** og giver aldrig drikkepenge.
sentence.en: He is stingy and never gives tips.

næringsrig.explanation: "Næringsrig" means "nutritious", full of vitamins, protein and other things the body needs. It is built from en næring (nourishment) and rig (rich).

sentence.da: Grønkål er **næringsrig**, fordi den indeholder meget jern.
sentence.en: Kale is nutritious because it contains a lot of iron.

nærmest.explanation: "Nærmest" means "almost", and also "nearest" for a place. Both meanings come from the idea of being closest: something that is nærmest a disaster is the closest thing to one.

sentence.da: Opgaven var **nærmest** umulig at løse på en dag.
sentence.en: The task was almost impossible to solve in one day.

nærværende.explanation: "Nærværende" means "present" in the sense of really being there with your full attention, not just in the room. In formal papers, nærværende kontrakt means "this contract".

sentence.da: Min læge er **nærværende** og lytter, når jeg taler.
sentence.en: My doctor is attentive and listens when I speak.

næseblod.explanation: "Næseblod" means "a nosebleed", blood running from the nose. Danes say it without a word for "a": Jeg har næseblod (I have a nosebleed). The doctor's word is næseblødning.

sentence.da: Når man får **næseblod**, skal man læne sig frem.
sentence.en: When you get a nosebleed, you should lean forward.

næsten.explanation: "Næsten" means "almost". Compare Jeg er færdig (I am done) with Jeg er næsten færdig (I am almost done). Do not mix it up with næste (next): næste uge (next week).

sentence.da: Jeg er **næsten** færdig med arbejdet.
sentence.en: I am almost done with the work.

næsten aldrig.explanation: "Næsten aldrig" means "almost never". It is built from næsten (almost) and aldrig (never). Aldrig already makes it a no, so do not add ikke (not): Hun spiser næsten aldrig kød (She almost never eats meat).

sentence.da: Han kommer **næsten aldrig** for sent.
sentence.en: He almost never comes late.

nødder.explanation: "Nødder" means "nuts" of all kinds, like hazelnuts and walnuts.

sentence.da: Egern elsker at spise **nødder**.
sentence.en: Squirrels love to eat nuts.

nødhjælp.explanation: "Nødhjælp" means "emergency aid", quick help sent to people after an earthquake, a war or a famine, such as food, water and medicine. It is meant for many people at once, not for one hurt person.

sentence.da: Efter jordskælvet sendte landene **nødhjælp** til området.
sentence.en: After the earthquake the countries sent emergency aid to the area.

nødig.explanation: "Nødig" means "reluctantly" and almost always sits after vil or ville (want, would) to say you would rather not do something. It is a soft way to say no to an idea. Do not mix it up with nødvendig, which means necessary.

forms.en: I would rather not go alone.
She would rather not say it.

forms.da: Vi vil nødig komme for sent.
forms.en: We would rather not be late.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **nødig** forstyrre dig, når du arbejder.
sentence.en: I would rather not disturb you when you are working.

nødt til.explanation: "Nødt til" means "have to" when you have no choice. It goes with at and an action: Jeg er nødt til at gå (I have to go). Compare it with Jeg vil gå (I want to go).

forms.da: jeg er nødt til at gå
du er nødt til at vente
vi er nødt til at tale

sentence.da: Jeg er **nødt til** at gå nu.
sentence.en: I have to go now.

nødvendig.explanation: "Nødvendig" means "necessary". It is stronger than vigtig (important) and means you cannot do without it.

sentence.da: Vand er **nødvendig**, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: Water is necessary when it is hot.

nødvendigvis.explanation: "Nødvendigvis" means "necessarily" and is nearly always used with ikke (not). It says that something is not true in every case, so it softens a claim and leaves room for exceptions.

sentence.da: Den dyreste bil er ikke **nødvendigvis** den bedste.
sentence.en: The most expensive car is not necessarily the best.

nøgen.explanation: "Nøgen" means "naked", with no clothes on. It can also describe trees with no leaves: nøgne træer (trees with no leaves).

sentence.da: Han sprang **nøgen** i havet.
sentence.en: He jumped naked into the sea.

nøgtern.explanation: "Nøgtern" means "matter-of-fact" or "sober": calm and plain, without drama or strong feelings. It describes how someone speaks or judges something. For "not drunk", ædru (sober) is the usual word.

sentence.da: Han gav en **nøgtern** beskrivelse af ulykken og overdrev ikke.
sentence.en: He gave a matter-of-fact description of the accident and did not exaggerate.

nøjagtig.explanation: "Nøjagtig" means "exact" or "accurate", with no mistakes: Klokken er nøjagtigt tolv (It is exactly twelve o'clock). Said alone, Nøjagtigt! means "Exactly!"

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **nøjagtig** måling.
sentence.en: We need an exact measurement.

nøjagtigt.explanation: "Nøjagtigt" means "exactly", with no difference at all in time, size or amount. It is the strict opposite of omtrent (roughly): nøjagtigt tre (exactly three) or omtrent tre (about three).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge **nøjagtigt** to hundrede gram mel.
sentence.en: You must use exactly two hundred grams of flour.

nøje.explanation: "Nøje" means "closely" or "carefully": with exact attention to every detail. It usually comes after the thing you do, such as reading, following or checking. Do not mix it up with nær (close), which is about distance.

forms.en: It does not matter that much

sentence.da: Man skal studere planen **nøje**, før man skriver under.
sentence.en: You must study the plan closely before you sign.
